title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #17

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's left hand? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North
   C. West
   D. South

2. On a county sketch map, what does the north arrow show? (1 mark)
   A. The rainfall
   B. The direction of north
   C. The number of people
   D. The size of the county

3. Which county contains the capital city of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru
   B. Nairobi
   C. Kisumu
   D. Kitui

4. What is a neighbouring county? (1 mark)
   A. A county that shares a boundary with your county
   B. A county in another country
   C. A county with the same name
   D. The biggest county

5. Which county has a neighbouring county called Kiambu to its north? (1 mark)
   A. Mombasa
   B. Kisumu
   C. Turkana
   D. Nairobi

6. Which of these counties has a coast on the Indian Ocean? (1 mark)
   A. Kilifi
   B. Nyeri
   C. Nakuru
   D. Kitui

7. What is a valley? (1 mark)
   A. A very high peak
   B. Low land between hills or mountains
   C. A big lake
   D. A huge flat plain

8. Which of these is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A bridge
   B. A school
   C. A lake
   D. A road

9. Which season usually follows the long rains in Kenya's common pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Long rains again
   B. Cool or cold season
   C. Short rains
   D. Hot season

10. Why is it dangerous to cross a flooded road? (1 mark)
   A. The road is shorter
   B. Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   C. Water is always clean
   D. There is no traffic

11. Which of these places is likely to be coldest in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The slopes of Mount Kenya
   B. A beach
   C. A low dry plain
   D. The coast

12. Which of these is most likely to happen in the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers fill with water
   B. Grass dries up completely
   C. Herders move very far for water
   D. Farmers harvest all their maize

13. Which of these is a service learning activity at a historic site? (1 mark)
   A. Selling tickets to friends
   B. Sweeping and collecting litter
   C. Building a fire
   D. Painting graffiti

14. What is trade? (1 mark)
   A. Buying and selling goods
   B. Growing crops only
   C. Building houses
   D. Playing games

15. What does interdependence mean? (1 mark)
   A. People needing and helping each other
   B. People living alone
   C. People fighting
   D. People doing everything themselves

16. Which of these shows interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. A man refusing help
   B. A child eating alone
   C. A woman sleeping
   D. Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor

17. In a shaded map, which shade usually shows the most crowded area? (1 mark)
   A. The darkest shade
   B. White
   C. The lightest shade
   D. No shade

18. Which is a reason why many people live in towns? (1 mark)
   A. No water
   B. No roads
   C. No schools
   D. Jobs, shops and services

19. Which is a good manner when interviewing an elder about culture? (1 mark)
   A. Refusing to listen
   B. Laughing
   C. Interrupting
   D. Greeting politely and asking permission to record

20. What is a motto? (1 mark)
   A. A school bag
   B. A school bell
   C. A class register
   D. A short sentence showing what a school stands for

21. Which is a way of conserving forests? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the forest
   B. Cutting all trees
   C. Planting more trees than we cut
   D. Building fires

22. Where is titanium mined in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Nyeri
   B. Nakuru
   C. Kwale
   D. Kisumu

23. Which factor makes a place suitable for a factory? (1 mark)
   A. No roads
   B. No water
   C. Good roads and nearby workers
   D. No workers

24. Why is teamwork important in a project? (1 mark)
   A. It stops others helping
   B. It makes work harder
   C. It makes the project fail
   D. It shares work and helps the project succeed

25. What is a cost? (1 mark)
   A. Money spent on the project
   B. Profit
   C. Salary
   D. Money received

26. What is income? (1 mark)
   A. Money received from selling
   B. Money spent
   C. Money lost
   D. Money borrowed

27. Which of these is a good digital citizen habit? (1 mark)
   A. Asking an adult before going online
   B. Sending mean messages
   C. Sharing passwords
   D. Talking to strangers

28. Which behaviour shows patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring the flag
   B. Laughing during the anthem
   C. Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   D. Damaging public property

29. What is bullying? (1 mark)
   A. Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   B. Playing together
   C. Sharing food
   D. Helping a friend

30. What is forgiveness? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring the wrong
   B. Punishing without listening
   C. Keeping anger forever
   D. Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you

31. What is female genital mutilation? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of sport
   B. A kind of food
   C. Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal
   D. A kind of school

32. What is campaigning? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing away ballots
   B. Counting votes
   C. Telling voters why they should choose you
   D. Announcing results

33. Which quality is important for a pupil leader? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Selfishness
   C. Honesty
   D. Laziness

34. Which shows respect for the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at them
   B. Following fair instructions politely
   C. Ignoring leaders
   D. Insulting leaders

35. Which activity can show leadership qualities in class? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   C. Copying
   D. Fighting

36. Which quality means telling the truth? (1 mark)
   A. Pride
   B. Anger
   C. Honesty
   D. Laziness

37. How many county governments are there in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 37
   B. 27
   C. 57
   D. 47

38. What does the county executive do? (1 mark)
   A. Prints money
   B. Makes national laws
   C. Carries out the laws and runs county services
   D. Trains police

39. What is a duty of an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. Issue passports
   B. Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   C. Command the army
   D. Run national hospitals

40. Who elects the governor? (1 mark)
   A. Registered voters in the county
   B. The chief
   C. The president alone
   D. The teachers

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between a physical feature and a built feature. Give one example of each. (4 marks)

42. County A covers 15 grid squares and County B covers 9 grid squares. Which is larger and by how many squares? Show your working. (3 marks)

43. Give four services provided by county governments. (4 marks)

44. Draw a simple chart showing three workers, what each gives, and what each needs. (3 marks)

45. Give three qualities of a good leader and explain why each matters. (3 marks)

46. Explain the difference between a chief and a clan elder. (3 marks)

47. Why do people trade? (2 marks)

48. State three duties of clan elders. (3 marks)

49. Explain four ways in which rainy weather makes roads dangerous. (4 marks)

50. Describe how you would make a poster on an economic activity in your county. (4 marks)

51. Explain why children must not be forced to do hard work. (3 marks)

52. Explain what would happen in a community if farmers stopped growing food. (4 marks)

53. Explain why we should be honest even when nobody is watching. (3 marks)

54. Describe how you would prepare a poster on the school values. (4 marks)

55. Give three things that should be on a sketch map of your county. (3 marks)

56. Give three factors that promote peace in school. (3 marks)

57. Explain how a class representative helps classmates. (3 marks)

58. Describe how to interview an elder about traditional culture politely. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — North
   Facing east, north is on the left and south is on the right.

2. B — The direction of north
   A north arrow shows which way is north so the map can be read correctly.

3. B — Nairobi
   Nairobi County contains Kenya's capital city.

4. A — A county that shares a boundary with your county
   Neighbouring counties touch each other along a boundary.

5. D — Nairobi
   Kiambu lies to the north of Nairobi County.

6. A — Kilifi
   Kilifi lies along the coast.

7. B — Low land between hills or mountains
   A valley is a low area between higher land.

8. C — A lake
   A lake is natural. The others are built by people.

9. B — Cool or cold season
   In the usual pattern, June to August is cool or cold in many places.

10. B — Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   Floods can carry people and vehicles away.

11. A — The slopes of Mount Kenya
   High places are colder than low places.

12. A — Rivers fill with water
   Rain fills rivers and streams.

13. B — Sweeping and collecting litter
   Cleaning up is a way of serving and conserving.

14. A — Buying and selling goods
   Trade is buying and selling.

15. A — People needing and helping each other
   Interdependence means we depend on each other.

16. D — Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   The farmer and tailor depend on each other.

17. A — The darkest shade
   Dark shades show higher numbers.

18. D — Jobs, shops and services
   Towns offer work and services.

19. D — Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   Politeness shows respect.

20. D — A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   A motto is a short saying of aims.

21. C — Planting more trees than we cut
   Replanting keeps the forest alive.

22. C — Kwale
   Titanium is mined in Kwale County.

23. C — Good roads and nearby workers
   Transport and workers matter.

24. D — It shares work and helps the project succeed
   Sharing roles makes work easier.

25. A — Money spent on the project
   Costs are expenses.

26. A — Money received from selling
   Income is what you receive from sales.

27. A — Asking an adult before going online
   Asking permission keeps you safe.

28. C — Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   Respecting national symbols shows love for the country.

29. A — Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   Bullying is repeated unkind behaviour.

30. D — Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you
   Forgiveness ends quarrels.

31. C — Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal
   FGM harms girls and is against the law.

32. C — Telling voters why they should choose you
   Candidates campaign before elections.

33. C — Honesty
   Leaders must be honest and fair.

34. B — Following fair instructions politely
   Respect includes obeying fair instructions.

35. B — Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   Role play shows how leaders act.

36. C — Honesty
   Honesty is truthfulness.

37. D — 47
   There are 47 counties, each with its own government.

38. C — Carries out the laws and runs county services
   The executive runs the county.

39. B — Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   MCAs represent their wards.

40. A — Registered voters in the county
   Voters in the county elect the governor.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A physical feature is natural, such as a mountain. A built feature is made by people, such as a bridge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct example.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: County A is larger by 6 squares.
   Working / marking points: 15 - 9 = 6. 1 mark for choosing A, 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for 6 squares.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health centres, county roads, pre-primary schools and markets. Accept cattle dips or water services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each service.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer gives food and needs clothes; teacher gives learning and needs food; driver gives transport and needs repairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct row.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty so people trust the leader, fairness so all are treated equally, and listening so decisions are wise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A chief is appointed by the national government to lead a location. A clan elder is respected by a clan for age and wisdom and keeps customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: People trade to get the goods they need but cannot make, and to earn money from the goods they produce.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep customs, settle disputes and advise at ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roads become slippery, it is harder to see, floods can sweep away people and vehicles, and water can hide holes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose one activity, draw a large picture showing people at work, write a title and two or three facts, and add one way of conserving the resource.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It harms their health, it stops them going to school, and it is child labour, which is against the law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: There would be a shortage of food. Traders would have nothing to sell. Prices would go up. People could become hungry and ill.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each consequence.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty builds trust, it is right, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the values, write a large title, draw a picture for each value, and use bright colours that can be seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: A title, a north arrow and a key. Accept sub-county names and boundaries.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Respect, sharing and forgiveness. Accept honesty, listening or fairness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: They bring classmates' ideas and complaints to meetings, tell the class what was decided, and help solve small problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet the elder respectfully, ask permission before recording or taking photographs, listen without interrupting, and say thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.
